title: Origin
paragraphs: “Ah, so saying that makes you show fear? I’d rather not use this tactic—especially since this is Elmero’s former family home—but… shall I declare the dissolution of the clan as the Shield Hero?”
“Th-that is—”
The other mammoths begin clasping their hands and bowing their heads in supplication.
“Shut up! How could I possibly accept such a selfish demand!”
“Well, wouldn’t it be best to just give it a try?”
“Grr…”
The old mammoth seems to be getting even more worked up.
“Well, I don’t consider myself arrogant enough to go that far.”
Just as Father was about to walk away after saying that, the panda spoke up.
“This is getting interesting. Well then, Elmero, why don’t you settle this in the Siltvelt way?”
“…What do you say, Elmero-san?”
Zou surveyed the mammoth family, starting with the old mammoth…
“As the Shield Hero commands…”
he replied, responding with a Siltvelt-style salute.
“All right, then… let’s settle this in the Siltvelt style—with a duel. If you win, I’ll grant any request you have as the Shield Hero.”

It’s said that Father was so taken aback by this bold declaration—thinking, “He’s gotten way too carried away!”—that he writhed in agony on his bed. It’s true that Father isn’t really fond of this sort of gambling. If anything, he’s the type to run the betting operations.
“You presumptuous, green-eyed brat! I’ll make you taste the consequences of your folly firsthand!”
The old mammoth roared that, driven by rage.
“I won’t… let that happen.”
Oh? The elephant’s tone has become a bit more defiant.
“Grr…”
Seeing the elephant show his resolve to fight, it seems the old man’s anger has dissipated just a little.
“In exchange, if Elmero, the knight I’ve chosen, wins… you’re forbidden from ever getting involved with her or approaching her again. You know what happens if you break that rule… right?”
“Don’t get too cocky…”
“Then go ahead and break my trunk. Isn’t that the Siltvelt way?”
“Grandpa, next time, I’ll be the one—Elmero Janon—to snap your other tusk right in two.”

Oh, the elephant sure speaks with some authority there. That’s a different side of him than usual. But I just heard something that’s got me a little curious. Was it you who snapped off one of the old mammoth’s tusks? I’m really curious about the details. Or rather, if you were capable of doing that, why did you just keep quiet all this time?
“Oh, oh… It seems the Wayward Knight has finally revealed her true form as the Queen of Earthquakes, hasn’t she?”
“That’s fine. I’m well aware I’ve been getting a little too cocky. But… I’ve finally realized there’s no need to be intimidated anymore!”
Zou claps her hands together, signaling she’s ready to fight at any moment. Then, with a thud, he stomped the ground particularly hard.
“Just how harsh Zeltoble is… the epithet ‘Queen of the Earth’s Tremors’… I’ll show you right here just how formidable it is.”
“Hmph… hmph! You’re so out of your league!”
“Fine by me. Come at me in droves—as many as you want!”
Zou’s tone is even more defiant than Panda’s. And so, we ended up watching the battle in the garden of the family estate where Zou grew up.

So, in response to Zou’s request, we joined the battle of Zou vs. the Mammoth Family… which turned out to be a fight against five mammoths. Talking big like that, only to rely on numbers… that really shows his true colors.
By the way, it seems the Flashy Mammoth has declined to fight. And yet he wants to serve as Father’s bodyguard? Isn’t that taking “not knowing one’s place” a bit too far?
“…You plan to take me on with just this many people? You’re welcome to bring more, you know? Hey, why don’t you join in too, Mom? You used to fight bravely back in the day, didn’t you?”
Zou provokes his mother—who certainly looks like his biological mother—by sweeping his ears back like a lock of hair. His mother is absolutely furious.
“Elmero! Stop getting so cocky! I’m going to get angry!”
“Don’t you realize you’re the one making me angry? To begin with, you’ve never once looked at me properly or shown even a shred of affection!”
Having apparently decided he’d had enough, Zou speaks bluntly. Yes, this is it. The pigs I rooted for were just like this. I could see a chance to win here.
“I’m sick of you only acting like a parent to mock me when the moment’s right or when I mess up. Come on, play by Siltvelt’s rules, you coward.”
“…You said it. I won’t go easy on you!”
“I’ve never gone easy on you from the start. I’ll never forget how, when I was little, you beat me up hysterically and locked me up until Lady Rainy came to my rescue.”

Whoa… how should I put this? Even among the complicated relationships of the pigs I know, that’s an exceptionally rough past to recall. And now, she’s striking back with a sense of catharsis. Elephant, go for it!
“I’ll kill you! I’ll kill you and completely wipe out the stain on our family’s name!”

Another mammoth has joined the fray. The prey’s got a huge hammer and all sorts of other dangerous stuff. It’ll be interesting to see just how many elephants they’ll bring in to overwhelm the opponent with sheer numbers.

However… it looks like he won’t show any mercy, even against his own mother. The mammoth—who seems to be his actual mother—is also showing a serious determination to kill. This is exactly what you’d call a battle between family members.

You can hear their ragged breathing—it seems the blood has completely rushed to their heads. Or rather… the garden is absolutely swarming with mammoths. Since they’re so huge, I’d like to watch the battle from somewhere with a good vantage point. By the way, it looks like Beastmen and slaves have started peeking at the garden from the roof of the mansion.

“Hmph. You seem to be getting a big head from that shameful job as a mercenary, but let’s see how far you can go against a group like this… The time has finally come to settle the score for the pain in my tusks!”
The old mammoth seems to be swinging an iron ball around. But will that really work against an elephant capable of handling Éclair’s attacks?
“Yes, I haven’t forgotten a thing. Including that incident at Lady Rainy’s funeral when you insulted her… Back then, it took four of you just to stop me, didn’t it?”
…So by that point, I was already putting up a good fight against four mammoths? Despite their appearance, these guys are weak.

“Hmph. I’ll say it as many times as it takes. The very fact that that sneaky, pathetic rat holds a seat among the nobility of Siltvelt is a fundamental mistake. To not understand that strength and power are everything—that’s the height of foolishness!”
“And what does a family of cowards—one that couldn’t win a single fair fight while that Lady Rainy was alive—have to say? You sure do bark a lot for a bunch of losers……”

It seems the elephant snapped off the old mammoth’s tusk because it was an insult to the dead old Beastman. But… that elephant sure seems to have a lot of pent-up frustration. He’s going to vent it all right here, in this arena prepared by Father.
“Shut up! I’ll beat you to a pulp so you’ll never open that screaming mouth of yours again!”
“Elmero, I’ll dispose of you—the stain on our family!”
“Seriously, you’re nothing but a nuisance… Taste the consequences of your own foolishness firsthand.”

Well, according to the story, his relatives—including his older sister and brother—have all declared they’ll kill Zou without mercy. Even at first glance… from his stance to everything else, Zou looks like the one who’s more accustomed to fighting. The way things look, this duel probably isn’t even worth watching.
“Hmph. Nothing but a bunch of paper tigers who can only charge.”
“Youuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu! You’re mocking me to the very end!”

By the way, in Siltvelt, “paper tiger” is apparently such a severe insult that it could get you killed. Unlike its original Japanese meaning, it’s apparently evolved into an insult meaning “loser,” used to scorn Hakuko, who was defeated in a past great war. So… Zou has put on something that looks like bracelets and anklets on both his hands and feet. Are those weapons? So he’s going to slaughter these guys with them! Hmm? I feel like I’ve seen those somewhere before.
“—Youuuuuuu!”
The mammoths all started radiating pure fury.
“It wouldn’t be fun if people said I won thanks to the Hero’s blessing, so I’m doing this to keep things fair. Come on, if you’re going to fight, now’s your chance.”
“What’s that?”

Father asks Panda and Éclair. I recognize it, too. Back when I was still foolish, I once spoke to an alchemist who was at the castle while Father was fleeing with his Finacée. It looks a lot like the bracelet—the tool meant to keep Filo-tan in her angelic form permanently. Unfortunately, I ran into Father before I could get it, so I never had a chance to use it. Is this a variation of that?
“It’s a bracelet that reduces abilities, isn’t it?”
“Ah, I see… Is it that well-known?”
“We use it when we’re not binding someone with a slave mark—like handcuffs or leg irons.”
“Whoa… Elmero must have been holding a lot in. To fight with the conditions lowered this much…”
“It’s refreshing—I like it.”

It seems Éclair takes a liking to the handicap Zou has imposed. On the other hand, the Mammoths must feel they’re being underestimated. They’re so angry, steam is practically coming out of their heads. But without a handicap like that, it wouldn’t even be a fair fight.
“If I lower the conditions this much… it’ll be about the same as before I was appointed a Guardian Knight. Come on, bring it on anytime!”
Zou said this with a more defiant attitude than usual.
“She’s really showing off the full dignity of the Queen of Earthquakes, isn’t she?”
“So that’s Lord Elmero as a fighter… It’s a world of difference from his usual self.”
“He’s not quite that provocative in real life, though. Still, it’s an interesting development—it almost feels like we’re getting a glimpse into the origins of his title as ‘Queen.’”
“Is there something to it? I just thought he was called ‘Queen’ simply because he’s strong.”

“Originally, she was called ‘Queen’ because she’s strong, but after she started being called that, she began putting on a show for the audience. Especially in death matches against monsters—she put on a good show, which went over well with the crowd, so the nickname stuck.”
As a spectator, this seems like a rather entertaining topic.
“I wonder if Elmero’s going to be okay?”
Kou is looking on with concern. Kou had expressed a desire to participate in the duel as well, but Zou gently smiled and declined, saying there was no need for Kou to join in.
“I think he’ll be fine. However… seeing him so worked up like that is rather unsightly. It’s neither elegant nor refined—it can only be described as barbaric.”
“Well, that’s just Siltvelt for you. The White Queen might not be able to understand it.”

By the way, thanks to her success in racing, Yuki-chan has earned nicknames like “White Queen” in various places, such as Shieldfreeden, due to the connection to queens. What was Sakura-chan called again? “Guardian Filolial” or “Gentle Filolial,” perhaps? What on earth is that supposed to mean!?
“Melromarc isn’t entirely without its own version of pre-duel verbal sparring… Fundamentally, hot-blooded knights and nobles tend to act similarly.”
Éclair seems to agree as well.
“It’s quite a bother, isn’t it? Couldn’t they just aim more elegantly—at the chest or head—and have the one who’s struck first lose, rather than this sort of duel?”
“That might work for a competitive duel… but when someone actually wants to kill their opponent, it’s bound to end up the same way either way.”
“I suppose it can’t be helped. It looks like it’s about to begin.”

Zou pulls a stone from the ground and raises it high above his head, as if signaling the start of the battle. Once that stone falls, the contest begins. Soon, the stone he’d raised so high drops to the ground.
“Take this!”
Six mammoths formed a formation, surrounding the elephant, and began chanting Magic. Meanwhile, the elephant, keeping an eye on its surroundings, also seemed to begin chanting Magic.
“Too slow! Is that all you’ve got?!”

The elderly mammoths finished their incantations triumphantly and cast their Magic spells in unison. Honestly… I felt like their incantations were quite slow. They were so slow, in fact, that they could have been easily nullified.
“‘Drifa Blizzard!’”
“‘Drifa Icicle Prison!’”
“‘Zweite Cold Shot!’”
The mammoths simultaneously unleash Magic spells of blizzards and ice at Zou. Layers upon layers of blizzard swirl around him, and in an instant, Zou vanishes into the storm.
“Hahahahaha! Now you’ll get a taste of the signature Magic of my clan—the very spell you’ve been dying to use but never could!”
Hmm… It seems the Mammoth clan, the Zou family’s ancestral line, specializes in ice-based Magic. I thought they relied solely on brute force, but this is an unexpected tactic.
“Huh… I thought you’d just come at me with fists, but you actually use some pretty unconventional attacks, don’t you?”
“Well, all things considered, it seems like a fairly renowned house even in Siltvelt. I’m sure they’re not just relying on brute strength and stamina.”
“Hahahahaha! Shield Hero, you’d better watch in silence as Elmero, the one you’re so fond of, gets frozen solid!”
“Well, I’m not so sure about that.”

Father seems completely unfazed by that old mammoth’s taunts, brushing them off as if they were the wind. Well, it was certainly an unexpected attack, but it feels like that’s about all he’s got. Then the old mammoth wrapped himself in a suit of snow armor. It looks like snow armor conjured by Magic.
